articles.headline: Dubois destroys Wardley in two rounds to retain title
keyFacts: Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley by a second-round stoppage to retain his WBO heavyweight title in London.
Dubois floored Wardley with a straight right in the first round before overwhelming him with punches in the second round, prompting Wardley's corner to throw in the towel.
The victory extended Dubois' professional record to 24 wins and marked his second successive stoppage victory over Wardley.
body: - Published
Daniel Dubois underlined his status as Britain's leading heavyweight with a devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain his WBO title in London.
The 29-year-old floored Wardley with a straight right inside the opening 20 seconds of their eagerly anticipated rematch at the O2 Arena and continued his relentless assault.
Wardley survived the opening round but was overwhelmed by another sustained attack in the second, prompting his corner to throw in the towel.
Dubois registers a second successive stoppage victory over Wardley, just five months after climbing off the canvas twice to dethrone his British rival in a thrilling 11-round contest in Manchester.
This time, there was no such drama for the champion, who was dominant from the opening bell as he extended his professional record to 24 wins - 23 by knockout - and three defeats.
"Fabio is a great boy, coming in for the second time, but it was my time and my era. I had my intentions, bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said.
"My back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did tonight."
Wardley, 31, suffered the second defeat of his 23-fight professional career.
Dubois comes out with intent in one-sided title defence
A sell-out crowd of 19,000 packed the O2 Arena and made their allegiances clear.

Wardley's charismatic yet measured personality has made him a popular figure. He looked full of purpose as he took his time on stage, fireworks exploding in front of him, his usual smile replaced by a look of determination.
Dubois, meanwhile, was greeted by jeers as he marched straight past the fireworks and towards the ring, wasting little time soaking up the occasion.
Actor Paddy Considine, comedian Rob Beckett, Oasis star Noel Gallagher and darts world champion Luke Littler were among the famous faces in attendance.

With 41 knockouts between the fighters, few expected the judges to be called upon. The feeling beforehand was that Wardley's best chance lay in making another fast start, having dropped Dubois inside the opening moments of their first meeting.
But in a stunning reversal, it took just 17 seconds for Wardley to hit the canvas as Dubois backed him into a corner and landed a straight right.
Chants of 'oh Fabio Wardley' were quickly silenced as Dubois continued to unload punishing combinations. Another furious attack towards the end of the round left Wardley in deep trouble.
Trainer Ben Davison, criticised for not withdrawing Wardley sooner in their first contest, stood poised with a towel in his hand as his fighter survived to the bell.
There had already been concerns over whether Wardley had returned too quickly after the punishment he absorbed in May, when he was left bloodied and badly swollen.

And those fears appeared justified as the challenger struggled to cope with Dubois' relentless pressure. Wardley's hands were low and his punches wild and telegraphed, lacking the menace he had shown in Manchester.
Backed into the corner again in the second round, he was subjected to another barrage before Davison leapt up and threw in the towel.

The two men could hardly be more different outside the ring. Dubois was typically reserved throughout fight week, looking uncomfortable in the media spotlight. Wardley, by contrast, was relaxed and articulate, insisting he had learned from his mistakes.
But despite their contrasting personalities and fierce rivalry, there was mutual respect at the end of the fight.
More to follow.

articles.headline: Daniel Dubois knocks out Fabio Wardley to retain WBO heavyweight title – live reaction
keyFacts: Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley via a second-round knockout to retain his WBO heavyweight title.
Dubois dominated the fight from the opening seconds, landing heavy punches that prompted Wardley's corner to throw in the towel.
Wardley stated after the bout that boxing is a game of fine margins and that he tried to adjust his tactics but it did not work.
body: As for victor?Dubois did not put a fist wrong. After hurting Wardley inside 30 seconds, he did not let him off the hook but was also – relatively – patient.
Dubois is such a sensational offensive fighter. It’s not just the raw power, he puts his combinations together superbly. He was unstoppable tonight, just as he was in demolishing Joshua in 2024.

“Wardley looked damaged from the first fight,” reckons the former world champion Carl Frampton on Dazn. “The punches that were hitting him early in the first fight weren’t doing him as much damage, as compared to this – his legs … he was hurt eight or nine times in four and a half minutes.”

What can we learn from that four and a half minutes of breathless brutality? Well, perhaps Fabio Wardley did take this rematch too quickly – only five months after all the damage he courageously he shipped in May.
Ben Davison, his trainer, was accused of being slow with the towel in Manchester – but he wasn’t tonight. He thought about it in round one, then called it in round two.
Frank Warren praises Fabio Wardley’s heart and courage – and he’s right.

“It’s never fun to lose – but it is what it is, it’s the name of the game,” says the defeated Wardley. “I’ve always taken on the biggest challenges … I tried to adjust some things but it didn’t work tonight. Boxing is a game of fine margins. I didn’t touch the canvas, so there’s a little bit of pride in that.”

He’s correct. Despite the absolute shellacking he took – hurt after 17 seconds and he never really recovered – Wardley did not actually go down. The ropes kept him upright, however, and his corner made the right decision to throw in the towel.

So much happened in less than two rounds there but it was all one-way traffic. Dubois pounced on Wardley from the start, hurt him and then was a patient predator – stalking his rival and opening up with hooks and power punches every time Fabio offered any resistance.
The man they call ‘Dynamite’ lives up to his nickname.
Absolutely brutal. Daniel Dubois does a peak Mike Tyson job on Fabio Wardley with a five-minute demolition. Wardley’s corner threw the towel in with their man shipping punches in the corner.
Wardley is trying to find Dubois with an uppercut – but he probably shouldn’t. Every time he does he gets crunched by hooks and power punches by Dubois… he has Wardley trapped in the corner. And…
Wow! Dubois returns the favour from fight one – he piles on to Wardley from the start, the referee decides only the ropes are keeping Fabio up and he takes a standing count.
Dubois in on the hunt. He’s crashing in jabs and hooks. Wardley is wobbling all over the shop! He barely makes it out of round one!
Both heavyweights get a pretty even selection of cheers as they are introduced – the crowd likely just want to see another action-packed contest. Will they get it? We’re about to find out.
Whatta Man blares and Daniel Dubous marches to the ring – he takes no time at all! Well, he wasn’t milking the moment. MC Thomas Treiber starts the intros – the first bell is only minutes away.
Fabio Wardley makes his way to the ring. “95% KO’s” reads a giant screen sign behind him, which may be statistically accurate, but we need to knock out that rogue apostrophe please.
Wardley is stone faced, all business. He raises a fist to the crowd and – despite being in enemy territory – gets a rousing reception as he steps through the ropes.
Sweet Caroline is being bellowed by the O2. “I think it’s going to be chaos from the first bell,” predicts Carl Frampton.
That first bell is imminent.
“Don’t Luke back in anger?” honks Colin Livingstone in response to my gag about Noel Gallagher and the world’s premier dartist being sat next to one another at ringside. Yes Colin!

At ringside, amongst the young and old hacks, the general consensus is that Dubois should win again tonight … but I’ve also heard a few people of decent repute say that they have a gut feeling that Wardley might just shock us and force an early stoppage.
It’s not long to go now and the arena is completely full. But it’s been strangely quiet so far – and even when Dubois and Wardley have appeared on the big screen there has been little reaction.
But if the rematch can replicate some of the drama and intensity we experienced in Manchester five months ago the atmosphere will be very different to its current lukewarm hum.
O’Doherty draws with Gomez Jr via majority decision!
Ouch. Michael Gomez Jr roars with delight as the final bell tolls – Louie O’Doherty looks downcast. But the judges have it to Gomez Jr by 115-114, followed by two scores of 114-114.

O’Doherty keeps his British and Commonwealth lightweight titles and Gomez Jr shakes his head in anger. He feels robbed of victory. The Mancunian certainly started like a steam train, O’Doherty battled back in the second half. But he may well be a lucky boy to get the majority draw.
Noel Gallagher and Luke Littler are in the posh seats and ready for the main event. “Little by Littler,” as Oasis almost sang. Does that work as a joke? Answers on a postcard.
Comedian Rob Beckett is ringside and says he wants “a proper humdinger” in the main event. Don’t we all?

Rob is getting a high-octane scrap here as O’Doherty tries to battle back against a rampant Gomez Jr – he’s battling his way back into this lightweight bouts, but is he fighting Gomez Jr’s fight? Possibly. We’re into the ninth round of 12.

Fabio Wardley looks cool as a cucumber as he speaks from his changing room. “I’m eager to get into the ring, eager to show off all the things we’ve been working on in the ring – eager to get my belt back,” he says, eagerly.
“There’s no pressure to do it early, late or whenever … a problem with the first fight is I tried to force the situation. I’ll just let it flow and come naturally.”

Dubois is an understandable pre-fight favourite tonight. But a word of warning: despite what Anthony Joshua might tell you, ‘Triple D’ does start slowly sometimes – almost like he needs to be clumped before he wakes up and starts boxing.
As was the case in May, Wardley will be aware of that and only too happy to supply the early clump if needed.
Meanwhile on the undercard: Gomez Jr has likely swept the first four rounds as he pushes forward with a relentless attack to body in head. O’Doherty began to return fire in the fifth. Good fight!
The final undercard bout has begun: undefeated Louie O’Doherty defending his British and Commonwealth lightweight titles against Michael Gomez Jr.
An all-action start from Manchester’s Gomez Jr in the opening rounds! Reminiscent of his dad, who always brought the heat.
Noel Gallagher and Filip Hrgovic are shown arriving, separately, at the O2. One of that pair will fancy taking on the winner of the main event … but which one?

It was surreal watching the referee refuse to accept the white towel flung into the ring to save Dan Garber from shipping further punishment against Adam Olaniyan, the promising young Irish heavyweight. Garber is 41 and it was bizarre to watch Amy Pu shake her head and kick the towel away. The next time the old heavyweight went down his corner pleaded with him not to get back up and Pu finally waved it off. It seems pretty obvious that a referee should always listen to a trainer who wants to protect a clearly beaten fighter.

Luke Littler, meanwhile, has just turned up and lingered awhile next to our row of press seats close to the ring. I’ve interviewed Luke before and he is not the easiest interviewee in the world and so, like all my other respectful colleagues, we left him in peace and didn’t ask for his Dubois-Wardley prediction.
The O2 is about 80% full – but it’s apparently sold out and should be jumping around 10.30pm or so when the big men walk to the ring.
“We’re going to see a special fight again,” predicts promoter Frank Warren, who was hardly going to say anything else. “The styles themselves will blend – and it’s got some spice to it.”

Fabio Wardley is getting his hands wrapped in the changing room. He spoke this week about using “a chisel instead of a sledgehammer” in terms of adjusting his approach – tweaking his first fight gameplan rather than starting from scratch. Sensible given his early success. But of course Dubois is bringing sledgehammer power.

Wardley has also accused Dubois of overconfidence in the buildup. Yet Fabio faces a tricky balancing act: on the one hand, he needs to box better than he did in May. On the other, his strengths are his power, stamina and superhuman durability.

The last thing he wants to do is get into a battle of the jabs with Dubois, who has superior footwork and fundamentals. So it needs to be high-octane brawling with a bit more nous from Wardley if he’s to earn revenge.

Easy does it for young Dublin heavyweight Adam Olaniyan. Dan Garber went down from a hefty right hand in round two, the towel came in from his corner … only for referee Amy Pu to throw it back out! She’s a hard taskmaster. Garber gamely boxes on but is soon pummelled back to the canvas and this time Pu waves it off.
Olaniyan moves to 5-0 and sounds delighted to have this experience under his belt.

Irish hot prospect Adam Olaniyan is next up as the heavyweight undercard action continues. It’s the 20-year-old’s fifth fight, taking on veteran southpaw Dan Garber. What a great experience for Olaniyan in front of a very full-looking O2!
Dubois v Wardley: tale of the tape. You know the classic meme of two identical Spider-Men pointing at each other? Well, both Brits are 6ft 5in, orthodox sluggers with a 78-inch wingspan.
Wardley (17st 10lb) is slightly lighter, while Dubois (18st 2lb) is two years younger at 29. But physically this pair are much of a muchness.

Fabio has a record of W20, L1, D1 (19 KOs), while the WBO champion has a ledger of W23 L3 (22 KOs). Wardley has gone the 12-round distance once, Dubois never has, but he does boast greater experience at this level.

Bakhodir Jalolov, the two-time Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist, continues his curiosity of a professional career by cruising past Solomon Dacres. Jalolov decked the brave Brit to the canvas in round five, but then was content to settle for a dominant 10-round decision.

The Uzbek looks to have it all: a huge, powerful, skilled southpaw. But he somehow fails to inspire. I can’t work it out. Anyway, he moves his pro record to a pristine 18-0. He’ll be a keen watcher of the main event.

Preview time: Donald McRae – who is at the O2 Arena tonight – has set the scene in style. Treat yourself to his analysis before the main event. Don will deliver some updates from ringside as the night goes on.

Five months ago, watching a likely Fight of the Year between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley in Manchester, a ringside seat offered an initially thrilling insight into the raw brutality of heavyweight boxing.

It was easy to be swept up in the drama as Wardley, defending his WBO title, dropped his more seasoned and favoured rival in the first and third rounds. But Dubois, whose courage had been questioned before, got up both times and fought back with admirable resolve.
The heavyweight action is already under way in London – unbeaten Uzbek amateur standout Bakhodir Jalolov taking on Britain’s Solomon Dacres in a 10 rounder.

Meanwhile, Daniel Dubois emerges from a sleek vehicle, wearing a tracksuit and an inscrutable facial expression, before wandering into the arena. Fabio Wardley has already arrived. The champ and challenger are here!

Tyson Fury versus Anthony who? Yes, Britain’s biggest-name heavyweights belatedly do battle in December – but if you want a better bet for an all-action fight, it’s tonight’s rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley for the WBO title.

The first contest was an astonishing slugfest in which Dubois was knocked down after 10 seconds, got dropped again in round three, but eventually bludgeoned a somehow-still-standing Wardley to defeat in the 11th. It was “like a Rocky film”, marvelled Frank Warren, a boxing promoter with no need to resort to embellishment.

The sequel takes place only five months later and a key question is whether Wardley has fully recovered from his brutal beating, which made for uncomfortable viewing by the end. The Ipswich man with the Cinderella backstory and a pugilist’s nose has shown mental fortitude and heroic durability on his rise from white-collar boxer to world-title level. Both will be tested as he looks to reverse his first defeat.

Strangely for such a wild brawl, Dubois’ jab was the key punch of the first bout. The Londoner used it as a ramrod to tee up his punishing right hand, whereas Wardley failed to set the table for power punches. “A victim of my own success,” reckons Wardley, who says he was guilty of overconfidence after almost stopping Dubois. “He’s not in my league, not on my level,” counters his rival.

Both Brits possess fight-ending power, as shown by their 41 knockouts in a combined 43 pro wins. Dubois has lost three times (once to Joe Joyce in an early-career upset, twice to Oleksandr Usyk) but appears dialled in now. Wardley’s only blemish aside from the defeat by Dubois is a draw with Frazer Clarke – but, Daniel be warned: he blew Clarke away in round one in a rematch to show his gift for self-improvement.
We expect ringwalks at around 10.30pm (BST). Then the in-ring fireworks soon afterwards. Do stay with us for live buildup and updates!

articles.headline: Valkyries have one big concern after WNBA Finals Game 1 win over Dream
keyFacts: The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday.
Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points for the Valkyries but suffered a late-game knee collision with Jordin Canada.
The Valkyries will try to take a 2-0 series lead when they play the Dream again on Monday night.
body: The Golden State Valkyries on Saturday survived the Atlanta Dream to win Game 1 of what promises to be a long, grueling WNBA Finals series.

Vakyries star Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points -- including 16 in the second quarter -- as Golden State held on for a 68-64 win at Chase Center, in the first WNBA Finals game held inside a raucous Ballhalla.
But a late collision between Williams and Dream guard Jordin Canada prompted concern for Golden State, and her status going forward will be something to monitor.
After she sank a pair of free throws with 2:15 to go in the fourth quarter, Williams fell to the court after Canada boxed her out at the free throw line.

Williams got up gingerly while massaging her left knee. The Defensive Player of the Year runner-up was in visible pain over the next couple of possessions before she received treatment on the Valkyries bench during a timeout.
Gabby Williams limping and in discomfort after collision with Jordin Canada. https://t.co/6pP3zw1GG2
— Underdog WNBA (@UnderdogWNBA) October 17, 2026

Williams seemed to walk off the pain and drained two more free throws with 4.1 seconds left to close out the win. It is highly unlikely that she will miss any time given how much is on the line, but if she is hampered in any way, the knock-on effect to Golden State's offense could be significant.
That said, the Valkyries just pulled off a win in a game where they scored just 26 points in the second half thanks to their greatest strength: team defense.
Golden State held Atlanta to 32.1 percent shooting and erased a five-point deficit entering the fourth quarter by holding the Dream to just two made field goals in the final 10 minutes.
Whether Williams is limited or not, the Golden State defense will remain strong as the Valkyries try to go up 2-0 in the series on Monday night.

articles.headline: WATCH: Texas A&M HC provides update on junior wide receiver
keyFacts: Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko stated that junior wide receiver Ashton Bethel-Roman missed Saturday's game due to personal reasons.
Elko stated that the team is giving Bethel-Roman space to deal with the matter following his earlier return from an injury.
Bethel-Roman has recorded seven catches for 56 yards in five games during the season.
body: It wasn't all good news for Texas A&M football after a 41-0 shutout win on Saturday , as head coach Mike Elko provided an update on the Aggies ' talented junior wide receiver.

Ashton Bethel-Roman did not attend Saturday's home contest against The Citadel due to personal reasons and is being "given space" by the team to deal with the matter. This comes after Bethel-Roman dealt with an injury earlier in the year, before making a return back to the lineup recently.

He was named the starter at the beginning of the season, but has caught just seven passes for 56 yards in five games played through the first seven weeks. Bethel Roman has been targeted 15 times in 2026, which is fourth among the wide receiving corps, behind Isaiah Horton, Mario Craver and Aaron Gregory.
Here's Elko's update on Bethel-Roman in the postgame press conference via TexAgs :
Mike Elko on Ashton Bethel-Roman's status: pic.twitter.com/ezwFbUTJBv

— TexAgs (@TexAgs) October 17, 2026 Texas A&M's wideout group keeps getting lighter each week. Terry Bussey and Madden Williams are out for the year and Mario Craver, Marcel Reed's top target, has also seen limited action over recent weeks while dealing with an injury. Fortunately, rising stars like Gregory and TK Norman stepped up for the Aggies in their Week 7 shutout of The Citadel, hauling in 11 combined receptions for 182 yards and two touchdowns.

Bethel-Roman being out of the rotation is a massive hit for Elko and company. With multiple huge SEC contests rapidly approaching, the health and overall status of Texas A&M's offense, especially the wide receiving corps, could be detrimental moving forward.

articles.headline: Don't throw away your old PlayStation — Do this instead
keyFacts: Old PlayStations can be repurposed into media centers for streaming and physical media or stripped for reusable parts like controllers and hard drives.
Unneeded consoles can be sold to buyback sites, traded in at retailers, donated to charities like Gamers Outreach, or recycled at e-waste facilities.
Before giving away or selling an old PlayStation, owners should back up their saved data and perform a full factory reset.
body: Don't throw away your old PlayStation — Do this instead
It doesn't need to end up in a landfill.

It can be sad to watch the PlayStation you spent hours fighting the hardest bosses with eventually fall out of use. But the fact that you no longer use your old PlayStation as much doesn't make it useless. So, don't throw away your old PlayStation; you can find other ways to give it purpose.

Thankfully, finding practical ways to repurpose your old PlayStation console can be pretty easy. With the right steps and a few hours, you can turn your beloved old PlayStation into a media center for watching your favorite shows or reuse its parts, among several other things. And if you feel there's no use to be had, you can sell it for cash or recycle it rather than throwing it away. Even old consoles like the PS2 can still be sold for cash today, so anything's better than your old PlayStation contributing to the already bad e-waste problem.
Turn your old PlayStation into a media center

Your PlayStation can access media in three main ways. First, there are streaming services. You can load up your old PlayStation with your favorite streaming apps and services. How you download them varies depending on your exact PlayStation. If your console is a PlayStation 3, this route is mostly closed, as many major streaming services have already stopped supporting the PS3.

If streaming services don't tickle your fancy, you can turn to physical media. Old PlayStations even as far back as the PS2 can play DVDs with the same disc drives used for games. The PS2 tops out at DVDs, while the PS3 and PS4 can handle both DVDs and Blu-rays. So, if you still use discs, your old PlayStation can find new life as a dedicated movie player.

Beyond discs and streaming apps, you can simply play media from USB drives. Before you plug the drive in, you'll need to format the drive to exFAT (or FAT32 specifically for the PS3) if it's in NTFS, then move the media files into folders on the drive. On the PS4, you'll need to install the Media Player app first. Next, plug it into your old PlayStation and enjoy.
Reuse its parts
Your old PlayStation might not be useful to you anymore in its entirety, but there are certain parts that you can easily reuse. Namely, the controllers, cables and even the hard drive.

PlayStation controllers, especially the DualShock 4, are compatible with a wide range of devices, from phones to tablets to PCs and even some new-gen consoles. You can even connect the DualShock 4 to an Amazon Fire TV Stick and use it for cloud gaming or even as a makeshift remote. Your old PS4 controller can easily become a gaming controller that works across your devices. The PS3's controller (DualShock 3) has similar functionality, but it works with fewer devices and the connection process isn't as easy as the DualShock 4”s.

If you're willing to dig a little deeper and remove a few screws along the way, you can harvest your PlayStation's hard drive and convert it into external storage for your other devices and files. Sony designed the PlayStation's hard drive to be user-replaceable, so you won't need expert-level technical skills to get it out. Once it's out, all you need is a quick reformatting and a USB enclosure for the drive, and you're good to go. Since you're putting the console out of commission anyway, you might as well repurpose the HDMI and power cables, too. Once you've pulled the parts you want, recycle what's left of the console responsibly.
Sell your old PlayStation

Yes, even your old PlayStation console can still be worth money if you know where to sell it. Selling your old PlayStation is a great way to get cash while getting rid of a console you no longer use, and, for most people, there are three main ways to go about this.

First and probably the most popular is trading in your PlayStation to retailers like Best Buy, Amazon and GameStop. This is the most convenient way to sell your PlayStation, but that convenience comes at a cost. For one, you'll get lowball offers, and most big-box retailers only pay out with store credit, which isn't that helpful if you don't plan on shopping there.

The second option is buyback sites like Back Market Trade-in. As the name implies, these companies buy used tech, including PlayStation consoles, for cash, with no listing or haggling involved. The upside is they're convenient, pay actual cash and typically value old PlayStations more than big-box retailers. But there are shipping risks, and you'll have to wait longer to get paid compared to retailer trade-in.

The third option is selling your PlayStation on marketplaces like Swappa and eBay. With this method, you stand to gain more from your old PlayStation compared with buybacks and big-box retailers. But handling a marketplace sale is typically inconvenient, takes longer and is more tasking than you'd encounter selling to a buyback or a big-box retailer.

So, sell on a marketplace if you want the most cash for your old PlayStation, sell to a big-box retailer if you want the most convenient option and sell to a buyback if you want a middle ground. Buyback will get you a better offer than big-box retailers while still being more convenient than selling on a marketplace.
Hand it down, donate or recycle your old PlayStation

If your PlayStation console no longer has a place in your setup and you feel it's not worth selling, then it might be time for ownership to change hands. Instead of throwing it away, you can hand it down to a younger person who'd give your old PlayStation the love and care it deserves.

If you don't have anyone to hand it down to, then donating it is your next best option. There are a number of charity organizations that can put your old PlayStation to good use and get it to people who'd appreciate it. Gamers Outreach, for example, collects certain donated consoles and gives them to children at hospitals. Before you send off your PlayStation as a donation to any organization, make sure to do your due diligence; check their online profile and reviews from other donors. Even old PlayStation consoles still have monetary value, so scammers can pose as charities when they're actually resellers.

If donating and handing it down won't cut it for you, or your PlayStation is too damaged for anyone to use, then recycle it responsibly using a local e-waste facility. Old electronics, including PlayStation consoles, contain hazardous substances like lead that can poison the environment if not disposed of properly. Fortunately, a number of large retailers like Best Buy and Staples have recycling programs for old electronics. Alternatively, you can use Earth911 to search for local recyclers around you.
Back up and reset your old PlayStation before letting it go

If you're giving away or selling your old PlayStation, it's best to back up your data (even if you think you don't need it anymore) then initialize (factory reset), so the console has a fresh start wherever it ends up while your data stays safe.

On a PS4, plug in the USB drive and make sure its file system is FAT32 or exFAT, not NTFS. Next, go to Settings > Application Saved Data Management > Saved Data in System Storage > Copy to USB Storage Device, then pick the saves you want to back up. If you subscribe to PlayStation Plus (and plan to continue subscribing), select Upload in the same menu to back up your game data to PlayStation's cloud storage.

On a PS3, plug in a USB drive formatted as FAT32. Then go to Settings > System Settings > Backup Utility > Back Up. Similar to the PS4, PlayStation Plus members can upload game saves to PlayStation's cloud through the Saved Data Utility in the Game menu.
Before moving on, PS4 owners should unlink the console from their PlayStation account. Go to Settings > Account Management > Activate as Your Primary PS4 > Deactivate.

Lastly, initialize (reset) your old PlayStation console. PS4 users: go to Settings > Initialization > Initialize PS4 > Full. PS3 owners: go to Settings > System Settings > Restore PS3 System > Read the warning and select Yes > Full Format.
Once that's done, your old PlayStation's software will look as good as new and be ready for its next purpose.

articles.headline: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
keyFacts: Rangers drew 2-2 with Dundee after Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser.

body: Dundee vs Rangers; Scottish Premiership
Dundee 2-2 Rangers: Callum Jones scores second-half equaliser as Rangers miss chance to replace Celtic at top of Scottish Premiership

Saturday 17 October 2026 23:15, UK
Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.
Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.
The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.

"I thought Dundee's press was good, as expected, and we wanted to try and draw the centre-backs out at times and try and hit spaces and feed our wide players and try and get 1v1.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed slammed for ‘racist’ Columbia research paper he wrote concluding Arab women should mate with their own
keyFacts: Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed faces criticism over his 2011 study linking interethnic mating to higher preterm birth risks for Arab mothers.
Critics, including Senator Ted Cruz, condemned the Columbia University paper as racist pseudoscience.
El-Sayed, campaigning to be the first Muslim senator, suggested future studies examine interethnic mating and neonatal mortality.
body: Left-wing Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is being slammed over a resurfaced Columbia University research paper he authored with a “racist and eugenics outcome” that concluded Arab women should only breed with their own kind for optimal health outcomes.

El-Sayed — who has repeatedly called himself a physician though he never completed his medical school residency — warned in the 2011 paper published in the “Journal of Immigrant and Minority Health” of the hazards of “interethnic mating” — which he insisted increased the risk of children being born premature.
“Our findings suggest that interethnic mating may be associated with increased risk for adverse birth outcomes among Arab ethnicity mothers,” he stated, back then going by Abdulrahman M. El-Sayed.

El-Sayed began the paper, titled “Interethnic mating and risk for preterm birth among Arab American mothers,” with the bold claim that Arab mothers, “a growing ethnic group,” have “systematically better birth outcomes” than white mothers.

He said American Arab women were 16% less likely than white women to give birth prematurely, citing his own research from 2008, while omitting to mention that same study found the gap disappeared after adjusting for maternal and socioeconomic factors.

The research, funded in part by NIH grants, concluded that Arab women having children with white men was linked to 18% higher odds of preterm birth — below 37 weeks — and 24% higher odds of late preterm birth — between 34 and 36 weeks — compared to having a child with an Arab father.
The study found no statistically significant difference in very preterm birth, before 32 weeks, based on whether the father was Arab or white, but didn’t spend much ink dwelling on that finding.
Critics savaged the paper as pseudoscience.
“This is ‘science’ with “a pre-ordained racist & eugenics outcome,” wrote Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Tx.) on X. “Scary stuff.”
Others wondered what the radical Democrat’s real motivation was to even research the topic.

“Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s scientific research is…odd. Arab mothers who engage in ‘interethnic mating’ have worse birth outcomes than those who mate with Arab men?” ripped John David Haltigan, an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Buckingham. “Why research this?”
Under Sharia law, Muslim men can marry “chaste” Christian or Jewish women, but Muslim women can only marry Muslim men.
“The father’s ethnicity did not appear to affect pregnancy outcomes when the mother was a non-Arab white woman,” he noted in the paper.

The paper also shamed interethnic marriages, saying the researchers found “Arab ethnic mothers engaged in interethnic mating were less likely to be married, had higher maternal ages….were more likely to smoke than their counterparts who mated with Arab fathers.”
He also claimed, “it has been shown that individuals in interracial/interethnic relationships have increased stress….in turn increase risk for adverse birth outcomes.”
For the paper, he looked at data for 617,451 women in Michigan, “the state with the largest concentration of Arab Americans in the US,” he noted.

He compiled data from the birth records of the State of Michigan’s Department of Community Health, looking at 21,621 Arab women and 594,431 white women who gave birth between 2000 and 2005, using self-reported ancestry to determine ethnicity.
El-Sayed, 41, who argued throughout the paper against “racial heterogeneity,” is the product of Egyptian parents.
But he married a non-Arab woman. His wife, Sarah Jukaku, is Indian. They tied the knot in 2006 and had their first child in 2018. They have two daughters.
“So he, an Arab man, can mate interracially, no problem, but Arab women, in his scientific opinion, it seems, are better off staying within their own tribes,” slammed writer Katya Sedgwick on X.
“El Sayed exhibits great many third world attitudes that are repressive, violent, and incompatible with our way of life.”
At the time of his marriage, El-Sayed boasted that the couple was required under Islamic law to live separately for a year without consummating their union.
“The interesting thing about the Muslim perspective is that it’s a lot more serious,” he told The Michigan Daily in 2006.

El-Sayed, who is campaigning to become the first Muslim senator in US history, suggested at the end of the paper future researchers may want to “consider the effects of interethnic mating on risk for other adverse birth outcomes,” including neonatal mortality and birth defects.
Other research he conducted at Columbia followed the same theme, including one where he looked at “ethnic inequalities in mortality.”
He withdrew his medical school residency application before he would’ve started it, to pursue public health instead.

articles.headline: Metal band Genitorturers allegedly claims a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is coming, getting a dozen crusty nerds way too worked up
keyFacts: A Reddit user reported that the metal band Genitorturers told a crowd in Brooklyn that a Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remake is happening.
PC Gamer confirmed that Genitorturers played a show in Brooklyn on October 15, matching the timeline of the unverified rumor.
Commenters suggested the band may have confused the project with Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2 or acted on outdated information.
body: This one is thin, man, but it has to do with one of my favorite games of all time, while the circumstances of the rumor are just kind of neat and weird, even if it turns out to be nothing. User Few_Interview8222 on the Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines subreddit reported back from a Genitorturers show in Brooklyn, New York. Partway through the set, the band supposedly told the crowd that a VtMB remake is happening.

I haven't found any corroborating accounts of Few_Interview8222's story, but Genitorturers undeniably played at Brooklyn's The Meadows as part of their "Live + Lewd Tour" on October 15, which puts them in the right place at the right time. We've reached out to both rights-holder Activision (one of several, it's complicated) and Genitorturers' representation, and will update this story if we hear back.
Why would an industrial metal band started in Orlando in 1986 have this information?

In addition to a killer score by Rik Schaffer, Bloodlines featured wonderfully era-appropriate licensed tracks from metal bands—they were mostly used as diegetic music in the nightclubs and bars of Los Angeles. The Genitorturers track Lecher Bitch was the pitch-perfect theme of The Last Round, a downtown LA dive bar frequented by the Anarch faction of vampires.
What if they're wrong?

Multiple commenters on the Reddit thread point out that this could have been a confused, untimely, misinterpreted, or all of the above reference to last year's Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2. You could easily imagine a concertgoer mishearing something in that context, or a performer fumbling delivery of the exact information. It's the sort of almost-but-not-quite thing you might expect from an artist with tangential awareness of a secondary fanbase they picked up over the years.

A VtMB remake is also the sort of project you could see getting pingponged around between various actors and stakeholders: started, stopped, shopped around, etc. It'd be a situation ripe for collaborators on the periphery acting on outdated information.
What if they're right?

Rad! I think? It'd depend on who's doing it. More and more, I'm beginning to distrust anyone not named "Nightdive" when it comes to commercial remasters. See also: The recent Shogun 2 debacle and the fate of Deus Ex Remastered.

Bloodlines is such a wild, janky, PC gaming package that Nightdive is the only studio I'd trust to not only do a remaster right, but also to bring on legendary modder Werner "Wesp5" Spahl, the man who's been keeping Bloodlines alive with one of the most impactful unofficial patch projects in gaming. A more ground-up remake would offer equally daunting challenges, like matching the one-of-a-kind mood and look Troika managed to evoke.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Why should you care?

Bloodlines is one of my very favorite games and an incredible RPG that's well worth your time. To the uninitiated, I like to pitch it as an evolutionary missing link between 2D Fallout and New Vegas. Bloodlines boasts the open-ended design and reactivity of Fallout in 3D for the very first time (Bloodlines leads Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson were senior talent on Fallout 1).

Unlike New Vegas' wide open world, however, Bloodlines had a more linear, but still loose sequence of zones on a world map to explore. Bloodlines' Y2K, gothic, noir interpretation of Los Angeles is one of the coolest worlds ever presented in an RPG.

A Nightdive treatment would be my preferred outcome: build on Wesp5's work and compensate him accordingly, then make it more accessible on more platforms at a modest markup over the original game. Bloodlines 1 can be had for $20 on Steam and GOG, but it's practically always on sale.

Even if it turns out to be nothing, this is still just a neat, newsworthy little incident to behold—Genitorturers shouting out an obscure, beloved RPG like this 22 years later, and maybe getting a couple genre nerds like me a little too excited on the way.

Ted has been thinking about PC games and bothering anyone who would listen with his thoughts on them ever since he booted up his sister's copy of Neverwinter Nights on the family computer. He is obsessed with all things CRPG and CRPG-adjacent, but has also covered esports, modding, and rare game collecting. When he's not playing or writing about games, you can find Ted lifting weights on his back porch. You can follow Ted on Bluesky.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed remains close to terror-linked mother despite best efforts to hide her from campaign
keyFacts: The New York Post reported Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed remains close to his birth mother despite her past terror ties.
El-Sayed featured his stepfamily in campaign ads while excluding his birth mother, who previously worked for a designated terrorist organization.
El-Sayed denied having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, attributing the accusations to Islamophobia.
body: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has carefully curated a family narrative for the campaign trail that erases his terror group-linked birth mother for his white stepmom — even though he remains close to his “ummi,” The Post can reveal.

Biological mom Fatten Elkomy, 66, a psychiatric nurse at New Horizons Community Support Services in Columbia, MO, was born in Alexandria, Egypt, and previously worked for the Islamic American Relief Agency — a designated terrorist organization — according to 2010 federal court documents naming her.

While in Egypt in the 1970s, she was an activist with the Muslim Brotherhood — a terror-designated Islamist political movement seeking to establish sharia rule in Muslim-majority countries — according to a social media post from her own daughter, Eman Abdelhadi, El-Sayed’s half-sister.

His white stepmother, the former Jacqueline Johnson, 63, a Lansing-born mechanical engineer, is apparently far more palatable to Michigan voters. She and her parents, El-Sayed’s step-grandparents, were trotted out in two key videos the campaign has heavily promoted and even used for fundraising appeals.
“I wasn’t raised by my mother,” El-Sayed insisted this week when he was grilled by NBC Nightly News, as he campaigns to become the first Muslim senator in US history.
Yet when he’s not on the campaign trail, El-Sayed speaks affectionately of his birth mother, even praising her “uncompromising . . . way of doing things.”

The Michigan candidate was 3 when his parents separated, but Elkomy has remained closely involved in her son’s adult life — including attending his 2014 graduation from Columbia University’s Medical School, where the two are pictured sharing a beaming smile as they stand next to each other, along with Abdelhadi.
El-Sayed described his birth mother as “loving” and “devoted” in his 2020 book, “Healing Politics: A Doctor’s Journey into the Heart of Our Political Epidemic.”

“Both are strong-willed, charismatic, charming — and both are uncompromising, not only in their beliefs, but also in their approaches to life and their way of doing things,” he wrote of his mom and dad.
That year, he sent Abdelhadi money on Venmo for “Mama’s bday gift.”
And this past Mother’s Day, he revealed he had called her to wish her well, deliberately referring to her only by her first name in a post on X.
“Without you, I would not have been a mother,” Elkomy tells him emotionally in the call.
“Enjoy the day, and we’ll see you soon, ok?” El-Sayed responded. “Love you, Mama.”
Elkomy could not be reached for comment.
She made no public appearances on the campaign trail.

Besides the Mother’s Day post that didn’t show her face or her last name, the only passing reference came at a September 2025 Lansing stop promoting “Medicare for All,” where El-Sayed said, “my mother is a psychiatric nurse practitioner and my wife is a psychiatrist,” without identifying her.

Meanwhile, in a June campaign video he captioned, “I proudly endorse this message from my grandparents,” with a heart emoji, his white step-grandparents give him a ringing endorsement, with the clip noting their US “roots trace back to the early 1800s.”

“Where did Abdul El-Sayed come from?” asks his step-grandmother Judy Johnson in the ad. “Here!” she exclaims, referring to the Great Lakes State. “We’re his grandparents!” she goes on. “He buys us groceries every week. . . . Take it from us. We love him and so will you.”

Another video he shared in July featured his stepmother, who took El-Sayed for her married name and converted to Islam when she married El-Sayed’s father. In the clip, Johnson’s hijab is carefully hidden underneath a large straw hat, as the two chat on a porch about what El-Sayed brings to the table.
“We are a society of immigrants, we are just people . . . you care about people,” she says, noting El-Sayed’s medical background. “If we could see each other as people, that’s very important.”

“Even if you didn’t always know what it was like to be a darkly-complexion kid with a funny name, you brought that empathy of knowing what it was like to be different,” El-Sayed tells her, before the two share an awkward hug.

His family ties are not the only facet of his campaign consistently evolving, according to critics — El-Sayed has also bent over backwards to shed the socialist label, stridently insisting he’s a “capitalist” despite endorsements from socialist powerhouses like Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT), “Squad” Rep. Alexandria-Ocasio Cortez (D-NY), who pledged $1 million to his campaign and joined him at three Michigan stops this week.

“Abdul El-Sayed has taken pains to hide his own terrorist-connected mother from public view because he knows her ties to Osama bin Laden, the Taliban, and Hamas are indefensible,” said RNC Spokesman Hunter Lovell. “If El-Sayed can’t be honest about his family’s troubling ties to terrorism, how can Michiganders trust him to have their best interests at heart?”

In addition to his family connections, El-Sayed signed a 2012 open letter calling on the Muslim Brotherhood to “purge” the press and police after the radical group seized control of Egypt, the Washington Free Beacon reported.

“Looking at his organizational connections, his family connections, his background is consistent with what one would expect from somebody with close ties to the Muslim Brotherhood,” said Kyle Shideler, director of Homeland Security and Counterterrorism at the Center for Security Policy.

Shideler noted both El-Sayed and his wife, Sarah Jukaku, were high-ranking officers during their undergraduate studies at the University of Michigan’s Muslim Students Association chapter, which was identified in a Muslim Brotherhood strategy memo among “organizations and friends” in North America.

“Muslim Brotherhood members typically keep things within the family. Membership will be something that passes on from father to son, mother to daughter. It’s very often common for them to intermarry. It often becomes their whole social circle.”
“He’s a Muslim Brotherhood guy, 100%,” President Trump said Thursday during a lunch in the White House Rose Garden.
“How about having him be on the Senate Intelligence Committee? How about that? The guy’s 100% Muslim Brotherhood. . . . He’s a fraud. He’s a con man.”
Even NBC confronted El-Sayed Wednesday on whether he lied about his family’s ties to the Muslim Brotherhood — a claim that has become increasingly difficult for the candidate to defend.
“Are you serious?” El-Sayed responded. “I have no ties. We have no ties,” he claimed, before accusing his critics of being Islamophobic.
“I have never had these conversations with my mother. I wasn’t raised by my mother,” he purported. “You’re using hearsay evidence from a tweet. It’s not serious. It’s just not serious.”
“Are you insinuating that somehow I was lying? I’m telling you I was not,” he went on, visibly agitated.
El-Sayed even cried racism during a campaign stop Thursday with AOC.
“I’m not supposed to run for office, I know that, alright? I got the wrong name for that,” he lamented.

“El-Sayed’s denials must also be considered in the broader context of how the Muslim Brotherhood operates,” warned Mariam Wahba, analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, and expert on the movement.
“It operates through a wider ecosystem of sympathizers, political allies, and individuals who share its worldview without necessarily holding an official position or carrying a membership card.”

El Sayed’s mom worked for the Islamic American Relief Agency from 1999 through at least 2004. She was named 14 times in federal court documents filed in the US District Court in Missouri in 2010, documenting her participation in eight wire transfers to the Middle East.

The Islamic American Relief Agency was designated a terrorist organization by the Treasury Department in 2004 for funding Al Qaeda and Hamas, accused of funneling “hundreds of thousands of dollars” to Osama Bin Laden” before 9/11.

Abdelhadi wrote in a 2012 post on X, “Had an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college #respect.”

“The Brotherhood wants to position itself as the leaders of Muslim Americans, which in turn gives them political power. It wants to prevent Muslim Americans from assimilating into American culture,” said Shideler. “It wants to use political power in the United States to support activities abroad.”
“Ultimately, at the end of the day, its big picture goal is to impose Islamic law on all nations everywhere and establish a caliphate.”

articles.headline: Rain98 is a blue-hued, pre-Y2K, Serial Experiments Lain inspired visual novel about time travelling to the past to end the world
keyFacts: Rain98 is a blue-hued, pre-Y2K visual novel demo about a suicidal present-day man who travels back to 1998 Tokyo.
The protagonist meets a depressed young woman named Reina Amehara, and the two strike up a deal to end the world.
According to the Steam page, the full game is scheduled to be released by the end of the year.
body: Picture this. You're me, and you boot up the demo for Rain98, an incredibly blue-looking, rainy visual novel set in Tokyo, 1998, about a woman who refers to herself as the Angolmois, a world-ending reference to the predictions of good ole Nostradamus. At one point you have to light this woman's cigarette in a lightly stylish sequence. You get to a bit where you're asked to put your name in, and you put it in because like its predecessors, this is surely a self-insert kind of situation. Only you get a Steam achievement for getting a game over for putting your name in. Rude! But curious, so you, and of course I mean I, pressed on.

In Rain98, you play as a nameless Generic Man who is deeply troubled, if not outright suicidal (of which this game has strong themes of) by the state of the world as it is in our present day. It's a fair stance to take! I would not exactly say things are good right now. But they weren't great in 1998 Japan, the year that Generic Man is somehow transported back to, finding this young woman, Reina Amehara, the Angolmois, in what he thinks is his apartment. She too is depressed about everything, and while the two don't hit it off at first, they strike up a deal: to end the world.

This Heisei-era ennui and nihilism is relatively appropriately placed too. It was a time of the lost decades, a period where Japan's economy massively stagnated, in turn influencing a wide range of strange, often anxiety-inducing and ominous works like Serial Experiments Lain, Neon Genesis Evangelion and All About Lily Chou-Chou. The first of the three is apparently an influence on Rain98, a touch you can certainly feel at least a little bit of in its vibe.

Quite quickly while playing the demo, I realised that this whole time travel situation is a pretty smart one. The world sucks now, and the world sucked then. How will these two characters from different parts of history respond to one another's inability to accept their material conditions, which aren't so different? That isn't an answer I found in the demo, I only managed about an hour of it and it runs a total of three hours, so I'm expecting to have to put a lot more than that into the full game.

Speaking of the full game, I didn't manage to experience all of what it has to offer either. There are seemingly a few different minigames scattered throughout, like one involving legally distinct DDR, legally distinct Tamagotchi, legally distinct Tekken, and more besides. Not sure if any of that can be found in the demo, but it all looks charming enough. I'm certainly won over by the demo so far, and if the Steam page sticks to its promises, Rain98 will be out by the end of the year.

Zotac said the system features an 850W power supply, supports up to six displays, and includes multiple connectivity options like Wi-Fi 7 and Thunderbolt 4.
body: - Zotac Magnus One Ultra’s Core Ultra 7 265 delivers 20 cores and speeds of up to 5.3 GHz
- Nvidia rates the desktop RTX 5080 at 1,801 AI TOPS for artificial intelligence workloads
- The desktop GPU features 10,752 CUDA cores, 336 Tensor cores, and 84 RT cores
Zotac has released a compact desktop computer built around Nvidia's GeForce RTX 5080, with barebones pricing starting at approximately ~ $2,640 in Japan.
The Magnus One Ultra EU275080C combines a desktop graphics card with Intel's Core Ultra 7 265 processor inside an 11.46L enclosure.
The 20-core processor runs at 2.4GHz and boosts up to 5.3GHz, and Zotac says the device is one of the smallest PC to pair a desktop RTX 5080 with a desktop Intel Core Ultra chip.
Desktop RTX 5080 power comes in a compact enclosure
The system uses Nvidia’s Blackwell architecture and supports DLSS 4.5 with Multi-Frame Generation, ray tracing, 4K gaming and local artificial intelligence workloads.
Its desktop RTX 5080 includes 16GB of GDDR7 memory, distinguishing it from compact computers that rely on integrated graphics or mobile GPUs.
The memory runs on a 256-bit bus with 960GB/s of bandwidth, alongside 10,752 CUDA cores, 336 Tensor cores and 84 RT cores.
Nvidia rates the GPU at 1,801 AI TOPS, and it is considered to be about 33% ahead of the RTX 4080 in games.

Nvidia also sells laptop RTX 5080 graphics hardware, but those mobile components are not equivalent to the desktop version.
Zotac fits the hardware inside a chassis measuring 126 x 365.5 x 249 mm, with a total weight of approximately 6.34 kg.
An 850W power supply supports the configuration, while the system offers two memory slots accommodating compatible DDR5 modules and a maximum capacity of 96GB.
The GPU’s 360W rating takes about 42% of that supply, and memory is rated at DDR5-6400 for CSODIMM and 5600 for SODIMM.
Storage expansion comes through two M.2 slots, supporting PCIe 5.0 x4 and PCIe 4.0 x4 connections respectively.
The connectivity options include Thunderbolt 4, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 and eight USB connections (four USB 3.2 Gen 2, four USB 3.2 Gen 1) for peripherals and external devices.
Display outputs comprise three DisplayPort 2.1b connectors, one HDMI 2.1b port, one HDMI 2.0 connection, and a DisplayPort-compatible Thunderbolt 4 port.
Together, these connectors support up to six total displays — or four simultaneous 4K displays driven directly by the dedicated graphics card.
With compatible displays and Display Stream Compression, DisplayPort 2.1b supports configurations reaching 4K at 480Hz or 8K at 165Hz.
The HDMI 2.1b output supports up to 4K at 480Hz or 8K at 120Hz, depending on the connected display and configuration.
Network connectivity includes one 5Gbps Ethernet port and one 1Gbps Ethernet connection, alongside a UHS-II SD card reader and audio inputs.
Barebones pricing leaves buyers to configure the system
Zotac lists several configurations, with Japanese direct-sale prices ranging from ¥418,000 (~$2,647) to ¥750,200 (~$4,750) depending on memory, storage, and operating system.
The entry-level package excludes all three, which means that users interested in this model will have to separately purchase the memory, storage and OS.
A version with 16GB of memory and a 1TB SSD costs ¥522,500 (~$3,309) with Windows 11 Pro installed.
The model with 32GB or 64GB of RAM and a 1TB drive costs ¥561,000 (~$3,552) and ¥654,500 (~$4,144), respectively, while the highest-priced option includes 96GB of memory for ¥750,200 (~$4,750).
There is also a Windows version of the Zotac Magnus One Ultra that comes with 32GB of RAM and two 1TB SSDs and costs ¥588,500 (~$3,727).

articles.headline: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
keyFacts: Meta updated its commercial terms to state it could use business account domain content to train AI models.
Legal experts expressed concern that the provision allowed Meta to scrape publisher websites for AI training.
Meta removed the language after stating the terms were meant only for ads and business products.
body: Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services.

According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab, this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.)
However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

articles.headline: Battlefield 6 Devs Respond After Players Take Aim at 'Secuty' Typo and Cosmetic With 5 Pistols
keyFacts: Battlefield Studios responded to player criticism on Discord regarding two controversial cosmetic items added in Battlefield 6 Season 5.
Developers stated that a typo on an armband will be fixed in November, while a skin featuring five pistols is an intentional creative concept and will not change.
Battlefield 6 Season 5 launched last week and will continue rolling out new content across three waves through December.
body: The Battlefield 6 team has responded after players took aim at a few controversial cosmetics added in Season 5.

Battlefield Studios took to its official Discord server to offer background information on two skins that caused a stir with the launch of Battlefield 6 Season 5 this past week (via MP1st ). The full text confirmed at least one of the issues has a fix in the works, while the other will seemingly remain the same.

The cosmetics – one with what appeared to be a typo in the word "security" and another featuring infantry sporting a whopping five pistol holsters – were officially added October 13 and almost immediately drew ire from fans . It's that pesky misspelling, which took the shape of the non-existent word "security" on the armband of a McNeil skin, that the developers say will be fixed when Battlefield 6 Season 5 launches in November.
Secuty 😭 It's AI
#Battlefield6 https://t.co/8DVphghCSU
— Battlefield Intel (@BattlefieldInte) October 13, 2026
"You called it out clearly, and we hear your concerns," the message, acknowledging the memes and conversations surrounding the new skins, said.

The note continued: "To be completely frank: Items that miss the mark like this do not reflect the quality standards you expect from us, or that we set for ourselves. We take pride in the craft of our world and our gear, and seeing visual oddities slip through is frustrating for everyone. We are currently examining our internal processes and workflows to pinpoint how these issues occurred and to see how we can tighten our quality control process going forward. Thank you for holding us to high standards."

It's a quick acknowledgement – and a promise for a quick fix – that should calm some concerns in the community. The communication from BF Studios and EA, however, did not address how exactly the typo happened in the first place or if there is any merit to the new generative AI accusations launched by fans in the aftermath.
💀 BRO IS CARRYING 5 PISTOLS! WHO APPROVED THIS SKIN? 😭
#Battlefield6 https://t.co/b6o94OkV1o
— Battlefield Intel (@BattlefieldInte) October 13, 2026

The other cosmetic that caught fans' eyes this week was the Midnight Mirage skin and its incredible five pistol holsters. It…felt like a bit much at the time, and its presence alongside the typo skin didn't do it any favors. Battlefield 6 players have kept the first-person shooter's outfits in the conversation since it launch last October, so mistake or not, an outfit like this was bound to draw some attention. As far as BF Studios is concerned, though, that design was not a mistake at all.

"This is an intentional creative concept—a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear," the message explained. "That said, we understand how this could look unintentional when released alongside other cosmetic anomalies."

That's where the conversation surrounding Midnight Mirage seems to end, so don't expect any of those pistols to be dropped anytime soon. The team then signed off promising to keep an eye on community response in the future.
"As we continue to try out new ideas to see what interests the community, you help us continue to evolve our cosmetics in Battlefield," they said. "Thank you for your continued feedback and support."

Battlefield 6 Season 5 launched last week and, like the seasonal content drops before it, will roll out over three waves. The first is already out and added the Vegas Strip and Area 51 maps, as well as a Dead Space crossover . New map European Casino will then arrive alongside a new event and tools come November 10. December 8 will see the addition of map updates for Blackwell Fields and New Sobek City, with more content and other changes also on the way.
IGN gave Battlefield 6 multiplayer an 8/10 review . At the time, we said, "With well-layered action and dynamic destruction, Battlefield 6’s multiplayer hits in all the places where it counts most."

articles.headline: Macron says violent rioters will be ‘prosecuted and punished’
keyFacts: Rioters attacked police, set fire to municipal buildings, and looted shops across French cities on Saturday.
French politicians claimed left-wing figures exploited student demonstrations concerning living costs and education to incite violence.
President Emmanuel Macron stated that rioters will be prosecuted, while elections are scheduled for the spring to replace him.
body: French President Emmanuel Macron released a statement on Saturday afternoon denouncing violent rioters who defaced national landmarks and attacked law enforcement officers in an escalation of protests that began last month.

“No room for violence in our Republic,” he said , referencing the increasingly hostile clashes between protesters and police that began largely as student-led protests about education policies. “Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted.”

Notable acts of violence broke out across Paris, Marseilles, Lyon, and other French cities throughout Saturday to protest the high cost of living, rising energy prices, and, at least in the protests’ original intent , understaffing at high schools and a lack of educational resources. Rioters broke into City Hall in Marseilles and knocked over a bust of Marianne, a longtime symbol of the Republic, while a tourism office in Lyon was also broken into and set ablaze. A town hall in the small city of Ligomes is “largely lost” after being set on fire, a top regional official told AFP .

“To the law enforcement forces, guarantors of the right to demonstrate, I express the support of the nation,” Macron also said. “We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who seek only to bring down our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so.” He had said last week young people’s “legitimate concerns” were being “exploited for political purposes and turned into urban violence.”

French Prime Minister Sebastian Lecornu said during the week the student movement was “instrumentalized by the allies” of left-wing figure Jean-Luc Melenchon, who attended a protest this week. France’s right-wing figurehead Marine Le Pen said the rioters have “poisoned” the original demonstrations “in defense of purchasing power.” Elections are scheduled for the spring to replace the term-limited Macron.

“Legitimate social demands have once again been held hostage by the far left and the speeches of Jean-Luc Melenchon’s deputies, who, by legitimizing violence, viewing order as oppression and disorder as a right, seek to plunge the country into chaos,” she said.
FRANCE GRIPPED BY VIOLENT STUDENT RIOTS ATTRIBUTED TO FAR-LEFT INSTIGATION

Firefighters and police were deployed across the country to put out the various fires and subdue the mostly masked protesters. Looters seized on the protests to loot stores and shops in Paris and other cities, according to AFP .
The protesters also vandalized a statue of Joan of Arc in Paris, according to videos on social media. The riots spread into other European countries last week, including Greece, Italy, and Belgium.

articles.headline: Villa's Manzambi shows Newcastle what they missed out on
keyFacts: Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi scored the winning goal in Aston Villa's 1-0 victory over Newcastle after turning down a move to St James' Park.
Aston Villa manager Unai Emery praised Manzambi's impact following his club-record transfer deal worth just over 50 million pounds.
Aston Villa will next host Norwegian side Viking in the Champions League before playing Manchester City in the Premier League.
body: - Published
Johan Manzambi saw first hand how good Aston Villa were last season and is now playing a crucial part in Unai Emery's rebuild in this campaign.

Switzerland midfielder Manzambi, who turned 21 on Wednesday, scored his third goal in Villa colours with the winner in a 1-0 victory over Newcastle - the club he turned down before moving to Villa Park in the summer.

Manzambi played a crucial role in helping Freiburg reach the Europa League final, before the Germans were comprehensively beaten by a Villa side that scored three times in the opening hour on their way to a 3-0 success.
Asked why he had joined Villa, Manzambi said: "The team was very good and I played against them in the final. It's a very good team with a big coach and that was perfect for me."
For Newcastle fans it was one that had got away, as Manzambi had looked set for a move to St James' Park before opting to join Villa in a club record deal of just over Â£50m.
Manzambi headed in the winner in the north east on Saturday, unmarked eight yards out when found by Joao Gomes' excellent cross.
It comes after he also found the back of the net in the 3-2 win at Tottenham and in the 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

"He has made a very good impact with his qualities," said a delighted Emery. "Skills and intelligence, both he has, and his physicality is very important as well to help us defensively and to help us try to keep the duels offensively.
"So happy he has scored another goal, fantastic for him."
One of the brightest talents in world football
Among players in the Bundesliga in his position last season, Manzambi ranked first for progressive carries of 10 metres or more (116), shot-ending carries (13) and fouls won (78).

He then impressed in the World Cup, scoring twice in the 4-1 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina, getting a goal and an assist in the 2-1 victory over co-hosts Canada and also registering an assist in the 2-0 success over Algeria.
Unfortunately for Manzambi and Switzerland, a knee injury ruled him out of the last-16 penalty shootout win over Colombia and their quarter-final loss to Argentina.
So impressive were his performances last season, that Manzambi finds himself on a 10-man list for the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the world's best player aged under 21.
Also on the shortlist are Spain World Cup winners Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsi, along with Yan Diomande - whose performances earned him a move to Real Madrid, with the winner named on 26 October.

Since his first start for Aston Villa on 19 September against Spurs, only Manchester City's Erling Haaland - with six - has been involved in more goals among Premier League players in all competitions than Manzambi's five (three goals, two assists).
Team-mate Nicolas Jackson, another to join Villa in the transfer window in a deal worth up to Â£65m from Chelsea, was quick to praise the youngster.

"He's an amazing player," said Jackson. "He's still growing. Hopefully he can be better and better every game, score goals and assist me as well. Hopefully we work together and achieve many things together.
"He will go a long way and hopefully gets no injuries."
While playing a crucial role in Villa's present and future, the team he has joined is a lot different to the one he played against in the Europa League final.

From the Villa side that won in Istanbul, six of them - goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, defenders Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa, midfielders Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers and striker Ollie Watkins - all left in high-profile moves, while substitutes Harvey Elliott, Jadon Sancho and Leon Bailey are also no longer at the club.

It proved a challenging start to the season for Villa as they only picked up one point from their opening four league games, but this win over Newcastle has extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to five matches.

As well as moving up to 12th in the Premier League, Villa have six points from two ties in the Champions League after thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 on Wednesday and are in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup, where they play at Bournemouth.
Botman challenge 'nearly broke my leg', says Jackson

Jackson has scored five times for Villa since his move and said he was lucky to avoid a serious injury when he was caught in the first half by Newcastle's Sven Botman, who was only shown a yellow card despite an over-the-ball challenge.

"I know the referee said yellow card but it was so high and hopefully maybe next time a red card, but it was a yellow," said Jackson. "I nearly broke my leg but anyway it's part of football. The most important thing is we win and we won, so I'm OK."

Villa entertain Norwegian side Viking in their third Champions League match of the season on Wednesday before hosting a Manchester City side that have won all seven of their Premier League matches this season.
"It was very important after our poor start [to the season] that we needed to try to come back feeling confident, feeling comfortable in how we are building our structure," added Emery.
"The players themselves tried to be demanding to change the situation where we are.
"Through the [Premier] league we are going to achieve our priority this year, so the league is the competition where we must try to be very consistent."
With seven points from their past three league matches, Villa are a side on the rise again.

articles.headline: The Mortuary Assistant Film Director Jeremiah Kipp Passes Away
keyFacts: Underground horror director Jeremiah Kipp has passed away, as announced by his partner Lindsay Katt and The Long Island International Film Expo.

body: Underground horror director Jeremiah Kipp has passed away, according to his partner Lindsay Katt. Confirmed through The Long Island International Film Expo, Kipp released his largest movie just earlier in the year, an adaptation of the hit indie horror game The Mortuary Assistant.
“Jeremiah was a gentle soul who was always generous with advice and sharing his knowledge of cinema,” writes the Film Expo, “he leaves behind many friends and an important legacy.”

Based on the 2022 video game, The Mortuary Assistant follows Rebecca (Kingdom Heartâs Willa Holland), a down on her luck woman hoping her new job will pave the road to recovery. Working grim but seemingly benign shifts at the morgue, she suddenly finds herself subject to strange visions. Thatâs when her employer, Raymond (Boardwalk Empireâs Paul Sparks), delivers the bad news. It seems a demonic spirit hitched a ride on one of the cadavers, and Rebecca will need to follow specific rituals to rid herself of the entity.

15 years ago Jeremiah Kipp made my dreams come true. I had a very dark and personal story about Suicide and he believed it needed to to be told. I got to write and produce "Crestfallen" as a film along side him. He became a mentor and a friend. Now he is gone and I am crushed. pic.twitter.com/bfc7ZBGQEo
— (NSC) The Beer Fridge (@PenningWyse) October 16, 2026

“Jeremiah brought his singular voice and passion to Dread through SLAPFACE and THE MORTUARY ASSISTANT,” posted the studio. “Our love and condolences are with Jeremiahâs family, friends, and collaborators.”

Shocked by his sudden passing, the New York horror movie community is mourning a man they describe as fostering with his time, passion and know-how. Before Assistant, Kipp filmed an array of indie nightmares, from shorts to Shudderâs Slapface in 2021. According to Deadline, the director had just wrapped production on Faceless, an upcoming horror feature based on Cambodian folklore.

The Mortuary Assistant was a crossover hit for publisher DreadXP, who had charmed indie scare fans with their Dread X collections but broke containment on the horror simulator hybrid. While it hasnât made as many waves as other recent adaptations like Iron Lung, it seems it performed well enough to assure the publisher. Elsewhere, DreadXP are expanding their cross-media operations, signing a deal with Blumhouse and YouTuber Matpat to adapt Amanda the Adventurer.

articles.headline: Photos: No Kings rallies in US urge midterm voters to cast ballots early
keyFacts: No Kings rallies were held across the United States on Saturday to urge early voting in the midterm elections.
Organizers said the events aim to ensure every eligible voter understands options for making their voice heard.
The Trump administration sued California election officials to bar counting mail-in ballots from suspected noncitizens until status confirmation.
body: In Pictures

Rallies organised by the No Kings network opposed to United States President Donald Trump were held Saturday in cities and communities across the US, with an aim of getting people out to vote early in the midterm elections.

No Kings has more than 3,000 events planned across the US. The planned events, this time dubbed “No Kings: Vote Early”, were billed as nonpartisan, though they sought to build on nearly two years’ worth of No Kings marches and demonstrations by people upset with Trump’s presidency.

“It’s a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard,” organisers said in a statement.
By advocating for voting early, the “No Kings” organisers hope to cut off the potential for any malfeasance once election day rolls around.

A band entertained what appeared to be a few hundred people in caps and coats at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC. Despite the chilly weather, many in the crowd danced to the tunes. “VOTE EARLY” and “HANDS OFF MY VOTE!” were among the many signs held aloft.
At an Atlanta rally, City Councilman Michael Julian Bond told the crowd to urge others to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.
“The Constitution gives you one power, right? That is the power to vote. Are you gonna use that power?” he said.

“You don’t see Superman giving up his power,” Bond continued. “You don’t see Black Panther giving up his power. You don’t see Wonder Woman giving up her magic lasso. So why would you give up your right, your power, your obligation to vote? Be a superhero, use your power. Go to the polls and vote.”
Trump has long been suspicious of mail voting and has claimed without evidence that voting fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election.

His administration sued California election officials Thursday, asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots for the midterm elections from people whom the federal government has identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed.

On Friday, the Department of Justice warned that local officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation and potential prosecution.

Earlier that day, Democratic Senators Alex Padilla of California, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island and Dick Durbin of Illinois wrote to Attorney General Todd Blanche, demanding that the Justice Department commit to not seizing ballots or other election materials before the midterm elections are certified.

articles.headline: No further action against government adviser's wife over Palestine Action post, police say
